title: What she played: Fats Waller, the player piano and family allowances
summary: She learned classics from a player piano, copied Fats Waller records, and was paid by her grandfather, uncle and stepfather to play their favourites; she still preferred jazz.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: At this stage were you just playing what people wanted you to play or were there certain kinds of things that you liked to play?

Well, I played anything they asked me to play. There were certain things that I played, like Fats Waller - I'd get his records. My stepfather bought me a piano but it was a what-do-you-call-it - set player? - style where you had rolls - player piano. I learned the classics from that.

The keys, my fingers would go down on the keys, yes... I had 3 people in the family - my grandfather, my uncle, and my stepfather, that would give me a weekly allowance to play their favorite tunes. My uncle liked Irish songs. My grandfather liked the classics and my stepfather liked boogie-woogie, so he'd give me more money than my - my uncle or grandfather would give me 50¢ a week and he'd give me 15 or 20.
You mean, if the one that liked classics had given you $25 -
A little more you might have ended up playing classical music?
I don't think so because I liked jazz.
